name: basic
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Canonical form, Fields, Defaults. A hash covers a section's definition.

name: full
source: Hand-written. Every field of every type is set, with a source and a section switch that must be left out, an env entry with an empty value, repeats in the two sets, and a section clause in an includeIf and in an askIf. Contract rules: the key order tables, Fields, Sets, Conditions. 0030: it excludes source. 0050: it leaves the switch out and hashes a section clause.

name: strings
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Strings. Quote, backslash, tab, carriage return, newline, other control characters, DEL, the three characters a JSON library may escape, and characters outside ASCII. The carriage return is in `owner`, which is not a prose field.

name: values
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Values, Conditions, Sets. The Value kinds are from the domain model. The Text deferred is the stored word from 0035, and differs from the Deferred kind. The isOneOf items are out of order on purpose.

name: unknown-fields
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Unknown fields. 0030: unknown fields are kept on a section. Keys are out of order in the input, and include digits, upper case, a non-ASCII letter, and a key that needs escaping. Decimals that a library may write with an exponent.

name: prose
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Prose. Every prose field is set, and the body holds a blank line, an indented line, and two spaces inside a line, all of which stay.

name: sets
source: Hand-written. Contract rule: Sets. docs/reference/section-template-schema/ordering.md: `after` lists the sections that must come before. The input is out of order with repeats, and the isOneOf items are of every kind.

name: switch
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: Conditions, Switch. 0050: a condition clause is a question clause or a section clause, and the hasher leaves the switch out. A section with enabled false. A section clause with enabled true and with enabled false, beside a question clause, in an includeIf and in an askIf, and alone in an askIf.

name: example
source: Hand-written. Contract rules: the Variable key order, Prose. A variable's example sits right after description. One variable has a description, an example, and a pattern hint. One has an example and no description. One has none. The second example holds a quote and a newline.

name: source-ignored
source: 0030: the hash excludes source. One section with no source, and the same section with three different sources, one of them empty.

name: enabled-ignored
source: 0050: the hasher leaves the switch out, the same as source. The same section with enabled absent, true, and false.

name: switch-enabled-ignored
source: 0050: the hasher leaves the switch out, and a section clause is not the switch. A section with section clauses and enabled false, true, and absent.

name: unknown-key-order
source: 0030: the hash is of structured content, so key order in the file does not change it. Contract rule: Unknown fields, keys in ascending byte order.

name: omitted-zero
source: Contract rules: Zero values, Conditions. Every zero field of a section, a variable, and a step is written out, and so are an empty includeIf and an empty askIf. The hash is the same as when they are absent.

name: defaults-explicit
source: Contract rule: Defaults. The domain model gives timing, type, and phase their defaults. Each default written out, alone and together, hashes like the absent field.

name: example-empty
source: Contract rules: Fields, Prose. An empty example is a zero field and is left out, so it hashes like an absent one. An example of only space, tab, and line ends is empty after the prose rule.

name: example-whitespace
source: Contract rule: Prose. An example is normalized like a description: CRLF, a lone CR, trailing spaces and tabs, and blank edges. The inner quote and newline of the second example stay.

name: prose-whitespace
source: Contract rule: Prose. Each of the eight prose fields gets whitespace noise at its edges or in its line endings: CRLF, a lone CR, trailing spaces and tabs, a trailing newline, and leading blank lines.

name: sets-order
source: Contract rule: Sets. `after`, `isOneOf`, and `isNotOneOf` in any order and with repeats hash alike.

name: list-order
source: Contract rule: Lists. docs/reference/section-template-schema/escalation.md calls `escalation` an ordered list, and the order of steps, variables, checks, run items, and options is behavior. Each other section swaps two items of one list, or repeats an item.

name: defaults-differ
source: Contract rules: Defaults, Conditions. A value that is not the default differs. A step does not take its section's timing or escalation, so a step with `timing: anytime` differs from a step with none. A condition with a clause differs from none.

name: section-clauses
source: 0050 and the contract rule Conditions. A section clause with enabled true differs from one with enabled false, from one that names another section, from a question clause that names the same id, from the same clause in the other condition, from a list with another order or a repeat, and from no clause.

name: prose-content
source: Contract rule: Prose. Only the edges and line endings are normalized. Inner spacing, indentation, the blank lines between paragraphs, a no-break space, and a form feed are content, in each prose field.

name: exact-strings
source: Contract rule: Strings. A pattern, a run item, an option, an env value, a directory, an open, an owner, a name, an id, and an unknown field keep every space, tab, and newline.

name: field-boundaries
source: Contract rule: Canonical form. Two sections with different content never share a canonical form. Text moves between neighbouring fields, items, and keys, and an unknown field takes the name of a known one.

name: value-kinds
source: Contract rule: Values. A Value is written by its kind. Absent, Flag, Text, Deferred, and List are all different, whatever the text inside them looks like.

name: unknown-shapes
source: Contract rule: Unknown fields. An unknown value keeps its kind, and an empty list or map differs from an absent key, because what it means belongs to a newer tool.

name: example-differs
source: Contract rules: Canonical form, Fields, Prose. Sections that differ only by example, from none, in a letter, in case, in inner spacing, in a line break, and in a final stop, and the same text in another field of the variable.

name: example-places
source: Contract rules: the Variable key order, Fields. An example belongs to its own variable and its own key. Moving it to another variable, swapping two, or writing its text as the description or the pattern hint gives another hash.

name: every-field
source: 0030: the hash is of the section's content, and it excludes only source. A change to any field of any type, except source, changes the hash, and a trailing space changes it in every field that is not a prose field. Contract rule: Fields.
